newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 23.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 23.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Wednesday to large shipping operations as a storm front headed toward the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.
Northern gulf ports Tampico, El Mezquital, La Pesca, Tuxpan, Veracruz, Coatzacoalcos and Nautla were closed to small tourism and fishing boats amid winds up to 45 km/25 miles per hour.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Clear skies and winds up to 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) with waves six to eight feet high. Weak cold front approaching and moving southeast at 28 km/16 miles per hour expected to cause lower temperatures, rain and winds up to 47 km/26 miles per hour.
The ministry said an oil spill will be simulated outside Lazaro Cardenas port on Friday from 0600 local/1100 GMT to 1600 local/2100 GMT for a mile along the coast.

Weak cold front hitting northern Tamaulipas state and moving southeast at 28 km/16 miles per hour, and drawing clouds and light rains along the coast. Winds about 15 to 20 knots with gusts up to 47 km/26 miles per hour and waves six to nine feet high, moving toward Campeche Sound later in the day.
Hot and partly cloudy with winds from 20 to 30 km per hour, clouds and rains said approaching with cold front. ((--Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903))
